facts.label: Entity and perimeter
facts.text: Perimeter matters for creditor claims. The balance sheet footnote states that consolidated VIE assets and liabilities of $2.3 billion and $1.9 billion at 2026-09-30 can be used only to satisfy the VIEs' obligations, with VIE creditors having recourse only to those assets and not to the registrant (10-Q Q3 page:7). Investment portfolio facilities are partly recourse to Holdco: secured credit agreements carry a 25% recourse guarantee from Holdco (page:47-48, page:50); the BMO asset-specific facility is 25% recourse (page:53). The Term Loan B is guaranteed by "certain subsidiaries" and secured by substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries (page:56); the guarantors are not named in the pack. The issuer, borrower, guarantor and restricted-entity map for the Term Loan B, the Revolver and the CLO issuers (a Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders and issuing banks is listed as an exhibit in the Q2 10-Q, page:133, but the filings do not say whether it governs the Term Loan B, the Revolver or both) is therefore an unresolved gap, not a conclusion. The subsidiaries exhibit is listed in the 10-K index but its text is not supplied (10-K page:173).

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The main story is balance sheet growth funded with debt. Total debt principal grew from 3,309,462 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 (10-Q Q3 page:89), an increase of 888,592 thousand, while total stockholders' equity fell from 1,068,023 thousand to 1,024,126 thousand (page:7). The company's own total leverage ratio, debt including the Term Loan B less cash over equity, rose from 3.02x to 4.03x (page:104-105). Most of the increase came in Q3 2026: the same ratio was 3.10x at 2026-03-31 and 3.32x at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q1 page:93; 10-Q Q2 page:102). Funding changed in kind as well as in size: the 2022 CLO was redeemed in May 2026 (page:43), and funding moved to larger secured credit agreements with Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman Sachs, a secured revolver drawn to 264,963 thousand, and a new 400,000 thousand Term Loan B that is fully recourse (page:56, page:89). The share of debt that is non-recourse CLO debt fell from 78.4% at 2025-12-31 to 45.7% at 2026-09-30 (page:77, page:89).

facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: Earnings are lower and thinner than in 2025. Net interest income was 76,067 thousand in 9M 2026 against 78,334 thousand in 9M 2025, because interest expense grew by 17,019 thousand while interest income grew by 14,752 thousand (page:7-8, page:102). Credit loss expense was 11,850 thousand in 9M 2026 against 2,594 thousand in 9M 2025. Net income was 41,437 thousand against 56,343 thousand. Q3 2026 was the weakest quarter: net income 9,366 thousand against 21,993 thousand in Q3 2025, credit loss expense 8,573 thousand, and Distributable Earnings of 5,118 thousand after a 13,006 thousand realized loss on a Plano multifamily foreclosure (page:39, page:81). Distributable Earnings before realized losses were 18,124 thousand against a common dividend declared of 18,508 thousand (release 2026-10-26 page:8). Loan credit metrics are otherwise stable on the face of the filing: weighted average risk rating 3.0 unchanged, no loan on non-accrual at 2026-09-30 compared with one of 41.0 million at 2025-12-31, and an allowance of 147 basis points of total commitments (page:34, page:37, page:88). The quality of the book changed in one respect worth carrying forward: office exposure was 4.3% of commitments at 2026-06-30 and 7.9% at 2026-09-30 after a 212.0 million San Francisco office loan was originated on 2026-09-24 (10-Q Q2 page:71; 10-Q Q3 page:72, page:116). The Q1 2026 release had said office exposure was below 5% (release 2026-04-28 page:2); that was a management statement about a point in time and does not describe 2026-09-30.

facts.label: Funding structure and recourse
facts.text: The recourse layer matters more than any single ratio. Applying the printed recourse percentages to principal gives nominal recourse exposure of 1,051,727 thousand at 2026-09-30 (Calculations), made up of 664,963 thousand of fully recourse debt and 386,764 thousand of partial recourse. Five percent of that, 52,586 thousand, is consistent with the 52.6 million of cash the company reports holding for the liquidity covenant (page:28). The same test is consistent with the 39.5 million held at 2026-06-30 (release 2026-07-28 page:3) and gives a requirement below the 15.0 million floor at 2025-12-31 (page:28) and 2026-03-31 (release 2026-04-28 page:3), when 15.0 million was held. This suggests the company holds cash at the covenant minimum and that required cash rises with each draw on recourse debt. The filing does not define "recourse indebtedness" and the match holds only on the basis chosen in Calculations, so it is an inference.

facts.label: Liquidity
facts.text: Near-term liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 291,634 thousand as the issuer defines it (page:105). It excludes contractual availability that depends on lender-approved collateral. Three points qualify the headline. First, 52.6 million of the 70,826 thousand cash is held for liquidity covenants (page:28), leaving 18.2 million available for investment (page:77). Second, the 87,317 thousand of secured credit agreement capacity is defined as available without pledging additional collateral (page:77), while maximum current availability is 777,844 thousand (page:47). Third, the 22,000 thousand secured revolver figure compares with an undrawn commitment of 110.0 million (375.0 million less 265.0 million drawn, page:77); collateral eligibility limits the difference. Against these, the company has unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand (page:71), of which 26,740 thousand fall due within a year (page:108), and unencumbered loans of 187.2 million that can be pledged (page:106). Contractual obligations due in less than one year are 3,000 thousand of Term Loan B principal and 26,740 thousand of unfunded commitments, plus estimated interest, for a printed total of 272,285 thousand (page:108). The secured credit agreement and secured revolver maturities used in the schedule fall in 2028 or later (page:57), so no facility is shown expiring within twelve months of the as-of date.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: TRTX is a REIT that originates and acquires floating-rate commercial real estate first mortgage loans, financed mainly by CRE CLOs, secured credit agreements and, since May 2026, a corporate Term Loan B and Revolver. It has no employees; its Manager, TPG RE Finance Trust Management, L.P., an affiliate of TPG, runs the business under a Management Agreement, and the chief executive officer, president and interim chief financial officer are TPG Real Estate professionals (10-K page:7-8, page:17). The creditor-relevant structure is therefore a levered, externally managed lender: income is the spread between floating-rate loan interest and floating-rate funding cost, protected in part by interest rate floors on the loans, and creditor protection depends on collateral quality, on how much of the funding is non-recourse or non-marked, and on how a manager paid on equity behaves as leverage grows.

In the quarter ended 2026-06-30 the company closed a 400.0 million Term Loan B and a 100.0 million Revolver, upsized the Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs secured credit agreements, closed a new 500.0 million Citi secured credit agreement, let the Barclays agreement lapse and redeemed the 2022 CLO (TRTX 2022-FL5) (10-Q Q3 page:43-44, page:48, page:55-57). After quarter end it closed a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, TRTX 2026-FL8, on 2026-10-02 and approved a new 50.0 million share repurchase program on 2026-10-26 (10-Q Q3 page:74). facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: In May 2026 TRTX closed a 400.0 million secured Term Loan B at a price of 99.75, bearing Term SOFR plus 2.75%, maturing May 2033, with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original principal from the last business day of December 2026. Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets of the company and certain subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 page:56). The filing says the Term Loan B and the Revolver are used "to repay outstanding indebtedness and for other general corporate purposes" (page:55); which indebtedness was repaid is not itemized, although the Q3 filing links the May 2026 redemption of TRTX 2022-FL5 to an upsized Wells Fargo agreement (page:44). At the same time TRTX closed a 100.0 million Revolver at Term SOFR plus 2.00% maturing May 2031, undrawn at 2026-09-30 (page:57). A Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders is listed as an exhibit to the Q2 2026 10-Q (10-Q Q2 page:133); the filings do not say which facility it governs and the text is not supplied. The company also paid TPG Capital BD, an affiliate of TPG, 0.9 million for capital markets services on these facilities (10-Q Q3 page:65). The management characterised the closing as securing "highly durable, non-mark-to-market liquidity" (release 2026-07-28 page:2), which is Management Language; the Term Loan B and Revolver contain no margin calls, but they are fully recourse (CP-1 handoff).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Investment-portfolio financing also changed in 2026. On May 15, 2026 TRTX redeemed TRTX 2022-FL5, which had 597.8 million of investment-grade bonds outstanding, and refinanced 17 loans with an aggregate unpaid principal balance of 698.1 million primarily through the upsize of the Wells Fargo secured credit agreement (10-Q Q3 page:43-44). The Wells Fargo agreement was increased to 850.0 million and its maturity extended to May 12, 2028 on May 12, 2026, with no margin calls for one year from that date; the Goldman Sachs agreement was increased to 750.0 million on June 30, 2026; a new 500.0 million Citi agreement closed on June 30, 2026; the Bank of America maturity extension to June 6, 2029, executed in January 2026, took effect on June 6, 2026; and the Barclays agreement was allowed to expire on its initial maturity in May 2026 with no borrowings outstanding (page:48). In September 2026 a 29.1 million first mortgage loan from BMO Harris Bank on the Plano multifamily property replaced an asset-specific financing after the underlying loan converted to real estate owned through a non-judicial foreclosure on September 1, 2026, which crystallized a 13.0 million realized loss (page:39, page:54).

facts.label: Governance and sponsor behaviour
facts.text: Legal capacity, willingness and feasibility are kept apart. Legal capacity: the board-approved investment guidelines and the covenants limit concentration and leverage, but the 10-K leverage expectation of "generally be less than 3.75:1" is an expectation, not a covenant, and the company reserves the right to adjust the range without advance notice (10-K page:15); the covenant maximum for total debt to total assets is 83.333% (10-Q Q3 page:57). Willingness: documented actions are dividends, buybacks and refinancing, with no creditor-adverse transaction. Feasibility: liquidity of 291,634 thousand and 52.6 million of cash held for covenants (CP-1 handoff). The overall behaviour reading is Neutral or Mixed on documented actions, evidence quality High. No score is stated.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. is a moderately leveraged, externally managed commercial real estate lender whose asset quality looks stable but whose cushions are narrowing. The strongest support is a senior, floating-rate loan book with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0, no non-accrual loans and commitments of USD 5,168.7 million, funded 78.8% without market-value margin calls. The weakest point is leverage: debt of USD 4,198.1 million against equity of USD 1,024.1 million gives 4.03x, above the 3.75:1 the company expected in its 10-K, with USD 52.6 million of cash tied up for covenants. What decides the outcome is whether loan repayments and the October 2026 CLO bring leverage and liquidity back toward the company's own range while earnings cover the dividend.

facts.label: Thesis
facts.text: The lender's senior, floating-rate, mostly multifamily and industrial loan book and long-dated, largely non-marked funding support its credit quality, but a rise in leverage to 4.03x, thin usable liquidity and dividend cover below one after realized losses leave a narrowing cushion that depends on repayments and refinancing execution through 2028.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. grew its balance sheet with debt in 2026, and that is the finding that matters most. Debt principal rose from USD 3,309.5 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,198.1 million at 2026-09-30, while stockholders' equity fell from USD 1,068.0 million to USD 1,024.1 million, so the company's own total leverage ratio rose from 3.02x to 4.03x and the debt-to-equity ratio excluding the Term Loan B from 3.02x to 3.64x. The 10-K had said the company expected total debt to equity to be generally below 3.75:1. On the ratio that includes the Term Loan B, TRTX is above that range; reducing net debt by about USD 286.8 million, or adding about USD 76.5 million of equity, would bring it back to 3.75x. The basis of the 3.75:1 expectation after the Term Loan B is not stated, so this is a pointer, not a breach [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: logged difference on leverage expectation].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The company's funding became more corporate and more recourse. A USD 400.0 million Term Loan B at Term SOFR plus 2.75% maturing in May 2033 and an undrawn USD 100.0 million Revolver closed in May 2026; both are fully recourse, as is the USD 265.0 million secured revolving facility. Together with partial recourse to Holdco on the secured credit agreements, nominal recourse exposure is USD 1,051.7 million, about 1.03 times equity, and the cash the company holds for its liquidity covenant, USD 52.6 million, is consistent with five percent of that exposure. Against this, 45.7% of debt is non-recourse CRE CLO debt and 78.8% is not subject to market-value margin calls [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity improved in headline terms but is thin in usable terms. Near-term liquidity of USD 291.6 million at 2026-09-30 compares with USD 143.0 million at 2025-12-31, but USD 52.6 million of the USD 70.8 million of cash is held for covenants, and only USD 87.3 million of the USD 777.8 million of secured credit agreement availability counts as available without pledging more collateral. After covenant cash, liquidity of about USD 239.0 million is about equal to USD 236.6 million of unfunded loan commitments [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings softened in the latest quarter and cover of the dividend is below one after realized losses. Net income was USD 9.4 million in Q3 2026 against USD 22.0 million a year earlier, and net interest income fell 5.7%. Distributable Earnings before realized losses covered the common dividend 0.98 times in Q3 2026, but after the USD 13.0 million realized loss on a Plano foreclosure Distributable Earnings were USD 5.1 million against common dividends declared of USD 18.5 million, a cover of 0.28 times. Over nine months of 2026 they covered declared common dividends 0.98 times before and 0.75 times after realized losses, while the company also bought back shares for USD 24.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures; CP-1A: Governance].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strength: collateral quality indicators. The loan book is entirely senior first mortgage loans, with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0 unchanged since 2025-12-31, no non-accrual loans, a weighted average loan-to-value of 65.9% at origination and an allowance of 147 bp of commitments. The mechanism is that senior, floating-rate lending with interest rate floors protects income and gives asset-level lenders collateral cover; the implication is limited realized losses so far (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Credit quality). The loan-to-value is an underwriting measure, not a current valuation.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strength: funding structure. 78.8% of debt is not subject to market-value margin calls, 45.7% is non-recourse CLO debt isolated from parent assets, the Term Loan B runs to May 2033 and the Revolver to May 2031, and secured credit agreement lenders are four banks. The mechanism is that forced deleveraging through margin calls is limited and term funding is long; the implication is lower exposure to market-value margin calls, although the secured credit agreements remain repurchase-style borrowings with credit marks (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse).

facts.text: Strength: disclosure and interest rate positioning. The company publishes a loan-by-loan schedule, risk ratings, recourse by facility and a liquidity table, and a 25 bp rise in rates adds about USD 2.9 million to annual net interest income because net floating-rate exposure is USD 1,186.2 million. The implication is good monitorability and a positive rate sensitivity (Documentary Fact; CP-1A: Company and operating model).

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weakness: leverage and thin equity cushion. Total leverage of 4.03x is above the 10-K's 3.75:1 expectation, equity fell 4.1% in nine months, and the indicative ratio of debt principal to total assets is 80.1% against a covenant maximum of 83.333%; assets could fall by only about USD 205.2 million, or 3.9%, before that indicative ratio reaches the maximum. The mechanism is that realized and provisioned losses reduce equity directly while debt is fixed; the implication is limited tolerance for credit losses before covenant pressure, subject to the unsupplied covenant definition (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Covenants, Calculations).

facts.text: Weakness: usable liquidity and lender discretion. Cash tied to covenants rises with each draw on recourse debt, secured credit agreement availability depends on lender-approved collateral, and unfunded commitments are USD 236.6 million. The mechanism is that liquidity can shrink when repayments slow or when the recourse base grows; the implication is dependence on repayments and the October 2026 CLO for headroom (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity).

The mechanism is that distributions drawn from equity reduce the cushion beneath creditors; the implication is that continued distributions at this level depend on earnings recovery (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures).

Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency: USD; the statements are in thousands of US dollars and the narrative and press releases mostly in millions. Question for this module: can the supplied source set support the requested downstream work (CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2, CP-5), and what remains blocked? ## Findings
### Reader summary

### Readiness view

The effective source set supports the requested work with limitations. All four requested consumers are assessed as READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS; none is CONDITIONAL and none is BLOCKED. The audited annual report, the three quarterly reports and the three earnings releases cover FY2025 and every quarter of 2026 up to Q3 2026, in the reporting currency, with the latest filing signed before the as-of date. The binding limitations are four. First, no executed legal document is in the pack, so covenant definitions, guarantor lists and security terms rest on filing summaries. Second, covenant levels are printed but the reported covenant ratio values are not; only a compliance statement is given. Third, no fidelity review of the text extraction has been done and no chart or slide was inspected, because the quarterly presentations are not supplied. Fourth, nothing dated after the Q3 2026 filing and release of 2026-10-26 is supplied. None of these stops a consumer from starting; each carries forward as a stated limit.
### Source-by-source assessment

All seven sources identify TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. as registrant or announcing company (page:1 of each 10-Q and 10-K; page:2 of each release). No source is blocked, draft or unsigned. The 10-K carries an audit report by Deloitte & Touche LLP dated 2026-02-17 (page:175-177). The three 10-Qs are unaudited. The filed 10-K and 10-Qs control their own facts; the releases are management claims that must not override them.

### Entity and perimeter

The registrant and reporting entity is TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc., consolidated with its subsidiaries and consolidated variable interest entities (10-Q Q3 page:11). It is "organized as a holding company" and operates mainly through TPG RE Finance Trust Holdco, LLC, which it wholly owns (page:11). It reports one operating and reportable segment (page:12). It is externally managed by TPG RE Finance Trust Management, L.P., described as an affiliate of the sponsor TPG (page:74; 10-K page:7); the Management Agreement is listed as an exhibit but its text is not supplied (10-K page:169). The context leaves sponsor blank; that is not evidence of absence.

Perimeter matters for creditor claims. The balance sheet footnote states that consolidated VIE assets and liabilities of $2.3 billion and $1.9 billion at 2026-09-30 can be used only to satisfy the VIEs' obligations, with VIE creditors having recourse only to those assets and not to the registrant (10-Q Q3 page:7). Investment portfolio facilities are partly recourse to Holdco: secured credit agreements carry a 25% recourse guarantee from Holdco (page:47-48, page:50); the BMO asset-specific facility is 25% recourse (page:53). The Term Loan B is guaranteed by "certain subsidiaries" and secured by substantially all assets of the Company and certain subsidiaries (page:56); the guarantors are not named in the pack. The issuer, borrower, guarantor and restricted-entity map for the Term Loan B, the Revolver and the CLO issuers (a Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders and issuing banks is listed as an exhibit in the Q2 10-Q, page:133, but the filings do not say whether it governs the Term Loan B, the Revolver or both) is therefore an unresolved gap, not a conclusion. The subsidiaries exhibit is listed in the 10-K index but its text is not supplied (10-K page:173).
### Period basis and version relationships

The pack gives a clean chain: audited FY2025 (with 2024 and 2023), then Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026 10-Qs. Each 10-Q is a separate active source; later ones do not replace earlier ones because they carry different quarter and year-to-date columns and the earlier ones hold the Q1 and Q2 balance sheets and covenant tables. The Q3 10-Q presents three-month and nine-month columns for 2026 and 2025 (page:7-8) and a nine-month cash flow statement (page:9-10). A discrete Q1 or Q2 2026 income statement is available from each respective 10-Q; the Q2 10-Q presents the six-month column. Cash flows are year-to-date only, so a discrete-quarter cash flow would need derivation downstream.

Each release repeats the same quarter's 10-Q numbers in summary form. Examples that tie: net income attributable to common stockholders of 5,820 thousand (10-Q Q3 page:8; release page:8), book value per common share $10.85 (release page:2), total allowance for credit losses $76.1 million (release page:3; 10-Q Q3 page:34), and near-term liquidity $291.6 million (release page:3; 10-Q Q3 page:105). No conflict between a release and its 10-Q was found. Distributable Earnings and Distributable Earnings Before Realized Losses are issuer non-GAAP measures (release page:7-8); the 10-Q also discusses them in Item 2 (page:76-81, page:110). Reconciliation to GAAP is given only at quarter level in each release; the nine-month Distributable Earnings reconciliation is not in the releases.

The context names FY2025 as the prior period. The 10-K supplies it with full statements and notes. No recast, restatement or discontinued operation appears in the Q3 10-Q; the 10-Q refers readers to the 10-K filed 2026-02-17 (page:11).
### Debt, liquidity and covenant evidence present

The Q3 10-Q gives, at 2026-09-30 and in thousands of USD: collateralized loan obligations principal 1,919,500; secured credit agreements 1,522,156; secured revolving credit facility 264,963; asset-specific financing 31,125; mortgage loans payable 60,310; Term Loan B 400,000; Revolver 0 outstanding (page:46, page:55, page:57). It also gives carrying values (page:58), facility-level commitments, maturities and recourse (page:47-54), the Term Loan B terms (Term SOFR plus 2.75%, May 2033 maturity, 0.25% quarterly amortization from December 2026, page:56), the Revolver terms ($100.0 million, Term SOFR plus 2.00%, May 2031 maturity, page:57) and a maturity schedule by year (page:57). Near-term liquidity is tabulated (page:105) and contractual obligations including estimated interest are tabulated (page:108).

The 10-Q prints covenant levels in two packages: investment portfolio financing arrangements (cash liquidity, tangible net worth, debt-to-equity previously, total debt to total assets and interest coverage; page:54-55) and corporate financing (total debt to total assets 83.333%, cash liquidity, interest coverage 1.3 to 1.0; page:57). It states that financial covenants were amended on closing of the Term Loan B and Revolver in the quarter ended June 2026 (page:55). It states compliance with all financial covenants to the extent of outstanding balances (page:55, page:57). It does not print the reported values of the tangible net worth, total debt to total assets or interest coverage tests: the test names appear only on page:55 and page:57, and the other covenant mentions (page:28, page:77, page:97) give the compliance sentence or the cash liquidity amount. The one covenant-linked amount printed is cash held to satisfy the cash liquidity covenant, 52.6 million at 2026-09-30 against 15.0 million at 2025-12-31 (page:28; page:77); the recourse indebtedness against which the 5.0% limb is measured is not printed, so that test's headroom cannot be read from the pack. Page:28 also describes Holdco as guarantor of the Company's recourse indebtedness. The reported debt-to-equity and total leverage ratios of 3.64x and 4.03x are printed (page:104) and are management definitions, not the covenant definitions.

Two availability measures coexist and must not be conflated downstream: "maximum current availability" under the secured credit agreements totals 777,844 thousand (page:47), whereas the company's near-term liquidity counts only 87,317 thousand of secured credit agreement capacity, described as liquidity available without pledging additional collateral (page:77, page:105). The secured revolving credit facility is described as $375.0 million with 264,963 thousand drawn (page:46, page:77), but only 22,000 thousand is counted as available (page:105). Undrawn commitment is therefore not usable liquidity.
### Latest quarter, subsequent events and contingencies

Evidence present for Q3 2026 and the period after it: originations of $772.7 million total commitments, repayments of $119.6 million and a foreclosure acquiring a multifamily property at $30.1 million (page:77); repurchase of 1,163,018 shares (10-Q Q3 page:8); a $1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, TRTX 2026-FL8, closed on 2026-10-02 with about $820.0 million of investment grade notes placed (page:74; release page:4), supported by exhibits 10.1 to 10.5 filed with an 8-K of 2026-10-06 (page:135); repayments of $72.2 million after quarter end (page:74); and a new $50.0 million share repurchase program approved on 2026-10-26 (page:74). The 10-Q states that the company was not involved in any material legal proceedings and recorded no loss contingency accrual (page:72). Unfunded loan commitments were 236.6 million (page:71). The 8-K of 2026-10-06 itself is not supplied. The release says a replay of the call remains available until 2026-11-10 (release page:4); that is a future date stated as scheduled, not a fact relied on. No event dated after 2026-11-05 is used.

Missing downstream analytical handoffs are not treated as source conditions. The dependency planner sequences them.
### Extraction status and fidelity

Every source arrived as text chunks and was read by search and targeted page reads. Tables arrived as flattened text, and column headers were checked against the period labels printed in each table. A successful extraction is not a fidelity review of every table, and none is claimed. The three releases refer to supplemental presentations hosted on the company website (release page:4 of each); these are not in the pack, so no slide or chart coverage is claimed and the presentation content is a parse gap, not a retained source.

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Funding and leverage grew sharply in 2026 while earnings softened in the third quarter. Liquidity is adequate but thin against promised loan fundings, and EBITDA-based metrics do not exist for this lender, so leverage rests on debt-to-equity. | Medium | No EBITDA is reported and covenant test values and executed agreements are not supplied, so coverage and covenant headroom cannot be measured. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Debt principal rose from 3,309,462 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 while equity fell, lifting total leverage from 3.02x to 4.03x. | Less equity supports each dollar of debt, and the new Term Loan B adds a fully recourse corporate claim. | High |

| Net income was 9,366 thousand in Q3 2026 against 21,993 thousand a year earlier; Distributable Earnings were 5,118 thousand after a 13,006 thousand realized loss. | Earnings only roughly matched the common dividend before realized losses and fell short after them, so equity is being drawn down. | High |

| Near-term liquidity was 291,634 thousand at 2026-09-30, of which 52.6 million of cash is held for liquidity covenants, against unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand. | Usable liquidity is thinner than the headline and close to the loan funding the company has promised. | Medium |

| The largest maturity year is 2028 at 1,130,841 thousand; 45.7% of debt is non-recourse CLO debt and 78.8% is not subject to market-value margin calls. | Refinancing is clustered in 2028, while CLO and non-mark-to-market funding limit margin-call risk. | Medium |

| No EBITDA is reported anywhere in the pack, and covenant test values are printed only as levels plus a compliance statement. | EBITDA leverage and cover cannot be shown and covenant headroom cannot be measured, so downstream work must use debt-to-equity and interest income cover. | High |
### Financial base view

The financial base is sufficient to support a credit snapshot of TRTX on a reported basis, with the limits stated here. TRTX is a floating-rate commercial real estate lender: 99.7% of loan commitments are floating rate (10-Q Q3 page:31), and loans held for investment of 4,916,375 thousand at amortized cost make up most of total assets of 5,242,861 thousand (page:6-7). There is no EBITDA, so the chart selectors for EBITDA leverage and cover are recorded as Not supplied and the leverage and cover analysis is built on the company's own debt-to-equity and total leverage ratios, on debt principal against equity, and on interest income against interest expense.

The main story is balance sheet growth funded with debt. Total debt principal grew from 3,309,462 thousand at 2025-12-31 to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 (10-Q Q3 page:89), an increase of 888,592 thousand, while total stockholders' equity fell from 1,068,023 thousand to 1,024,126 thousand (page:7). The company's own total leverage ratio, debt including the Term Loan B less cash over equity, rose from 3.02x to 4.03x (page:104-105). Most of the increase came in Q3 2026: the same ratio was 3.10x at 2026-03-31 and 3.32x at 2026-06-30 (10-Q Q1 page:93; 10-Q Q2 page:102). Funding changed in kind as well as in size: the 2022 CLO was redeemed in May 2026 (page:43), and funding moved to larger secured credit agreements with Wells Fargo, Citi and Goldman Sachs, a secured revolver drawn to 264,963 thousand, and a new 400,000 thousand Term Loan B that is fully recourse (page:56, page:89). The share of debt that is non-recourse CLO debt fell from 78.4% at 2025-12-31 to 45.7% at 2026-09-30 (page:77, page:89).

Earnings are lower and thinner than in 2025. Net interest income was 76,067 thousand in 9M 2026 against 78,334 thousand in 9M 2025, because interest expense grew by 17,019 thousand while interest income grew by 14,752 thousand (page:7-8, page:102). Credit loss expense was 11,850 thousand in 9M 2026 against 2,594 thousand in 9M 2025. Net income was 41,437 thousand against 56,343 thousand. Q3 2026 was the weakest quarter: net income 9,366 thousand against 21,993 thousand in Q3 2025, credit loss expense 8,573 thousand, and Distributable Earnings of 5,118 thousand after a 13,006 thousand realized loss on a Plano multifamily foreclosure (page:39, page:81). Distributable Earnings before realized losses were 18,124 thousand against a common dividend declared of 18,508 thousand (release 2026-10-26 page:8). Loan credit metrics are otherwise stable on the face of the filing: weighted average risk rating 3.0 unchanged, no loan on non-accrual at 2026-09-30 compared with one of 41.0 million at 2025-12-31, and an allowance of 147 basis points of total commitments (page:34, page:37, page:88). The quality of the book changed in one respect worth carrying forward: office exposure was 4.3% of commitments at 2026-06-30 and 7.9% at 2026-09-30 after a 212.0 million San Francisco office loan was originated on 2026-09-24 (10-Q Q2 page:71; 10-Q Q3 page:72, page:116). The Q1 2026 release had said office exposure was below 5% (release 2026-04-28 page:2); that was a management statement about a point in time and does not describe 2026-09-30.

Liquidity is adequate on the headline and thin on a usable basis. Near-term liquidity of 291,634 thousand at 2026-09-30 includes 70,826 thousand of cash of which 52.6 million is held to satisfy liquidity covenants (page:28, page:77, page:105). Unfunded loan commitments are 236,552 thousand (page:71). The covenant package changed when the Term Loan B and Revolver closed (page:55): the investment-portfolio debt-to-equity covenant of 4.25x is shown as not applicable currently, a total debt to total assets maximum of 83.333% applies, and the interest coverage minimum fell from 1.4x to 1.3x. The company states it was in compliance with all financial covenants (page:55, page:57), but the actual test values are not printed, so no headroom is reported as a company figure; an indicative balance sheet debt to assets ratio is set out in Calculations with its caveats.
Every figure below is a reported or derived USD figure on the TRTX consolidated perimeter. Statements are unaudited for the 2026 periods and audited for FY2025 (10-K page:175-177).

The recourse layer matters more than any single ratio. Applying the printed recourse percentages to principal gives nominal recourse exposure of 1,051,727 thousand at 2026-09-30 (Calculations), made up of 664,963 thousand of fully recourse debt and 386,764 thousand of partial recourse. Five percent of that, 52,586 thousand, is consistent with the 52.6 million of cash the company reports holding for the liquidity covenant (page:28). The same test is consistent with the 39.5 million held at 2026-06-30 (release 2026-07-28 page:3) and gives a requirement below the 15.0 million floor at 2025-12-31 (page:28) and 2026-03-31 (release 2026-04-28 page:3), when 15.0 million was held. This suggests the company holds cash at the covenant minimum and that required cash rises with each draw on recourse debt. The filing does not define "recourse indebtedness" and the match holds only on the basis chosen in Calculations, so it is an inference.
### Liquidity

Near-term liquidity at 2026-09-30 is 291,634 thousand as the issuer defines it (page:105). It excludes contractual availability that depends on lender-approved collateral. Three points qualify the headline. First, 52.6 million of the 70,826 thousand cash is held for liquidity covenants (page:28), leaving 18.2 million available for investment (page:77). Second, the 87,317 thousand of secured credit agreement capacity is defined as available without pledging additional collateral (page:77), while maximum current availability is 777,844 thousand (page:47). Third, the 22,000 thousand secured revolver figure compares with an undrawn commitment of 110.0 million (375.0 million less 265.0 million drawn, page:77); collateral eligibility limits the difference. Against these, the company has unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand (page:71), of which 26,740 thousand fall due within a year (page:108), and unencumbered loans of 187.2 million that can be pledged (page:106). Contractual obligations due in less than one year are 3,000 thousand of Term Loan B principal and 26,740 thousand of unfunded commitments, plus estimated interest, for a printed total of 272,285 thousand (page:108). The secured credit agreement and secured revolver maturities used in the schedule fall in 2028 or later (page:57), so no facility is shown expiring within twelve months of the as-of date.
### Covenants

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| TRTX is an externally managed, floating-rate commercial real estate lender with a TPG-affiliated manager. The filings give a clear business and funding picture, but no sponsor support commitment, executed agreement or ownership percentage is supplied. | Medium | Executed agreements, shareholder ownership percentages and the use of proceeds of the October 2026 CLO are not supplied, so governance conclusions rest on filings alone. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| TRTX has no employees and is run by a TPG affiliate that earns a base fee of 1.50% of equity; no incentive fee was earned in 2026. | Fees are paid regardless of credit outcomes, so manager incentives align with creditors only loosely, though other related-party fees are small. | High |

| In May 2026 TRTX closed a 400.0 million Term Loan B and a 100.0 million Revolver, both fully recourse, and redeemed its 2022 CLO. | Funding shifted toward larger secured credit agreements and a recourse corporate layer secured on substantially all assets. | High |

| A 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO closed on 2026-10-02, after quarter end, and a new 50.0 million buyback was approved on 2026-10-26. | The CRE CLO type is described as non-recourse and non-marked, but its use of proceeds is not disclosed; buybacks reduce equity while leverage is higher. | Medium |

| The portfolio is 52.6% multifamily and 22.6% industrial, almost all floating rate; office rose to 7.9% after a new 212.0 million loan. | Collateral mix is mostly multifamily and industrial, but office exposure rose in the latest quarter and one foreclosure shows transition risk remains. | High |

| The 10-K expected total debt to equity to be generally below 3.75:1, while the latest printed total leverage ratio is 4.03x. | Leverage is above the company's own stated expectation on one measure, so leverage tolerance and the basis of the target need confirming. | Medium |
### Business and transaction view

TRTX is a REIT that originates and acquires floating-rate commercial real estate first mortgage loans, financed mainly by CRE CLOs, secured credit agreements and, since May 2026, a corporate Term Loan B and Revolver. It has no employees; its Manager, TPG RE Finance Trust Management, L.P., an affiliate of TPG, runs the business under a Management Agreement, and the chief executive officer, president and interim chief financial officer are TPG Real Estate professionals (10-K page:7-8, page:17). The creditor-relevant structure is therefore a levered, externally managed lender: income is the spread between floating-rate loan interest and floating-rate funding cost, protected in part by interest rate floors on the loans, and creditor protection depends on collateral quality, on how much of the funding is non-recourse or non-marked, and on how a manager paid on equity behaves as leverage grows.

The transaction story is a refinancing and liability-management story, not a sponsor transaction. In the quarter ended 2026-06-30 the company closed a 400.0 million Term Loan B and a 100.0 million Revolver, upsized the Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs secured credit agreements, closed a new 500.0 million Citi secured credit agreement, let the Barclays agreement lapse and redeemed the 2022 CLO (TRTX 2022-FL5) (10-Q Q3 page:43-44, page:48, page:55-57). After quarter end it closed a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, TRTX 2026-FL8, on 2026-10-02 and approved a new 50.0 million share repurchase program on 2026-10-26 (10-Q Q3 page:74). There is no change of control, no acquisition of TRTX and no sponsor equity injection in the pack.

On the financial side, which comes from the accepted financial base and is not recomputed here, debt principal rose to 4,198,054 thousand at 2026-09-30 and the issuer's total leverage ratio to 4.03x, with liquidity of 291,634 thousand against unfunded loan commitments of 236,552 thousand (CP-1 handoff). Against that, the business has stable reported credit indicators: weighted average risk rating 3.0 unchanged, no loan on non-accrual at 2026-09-30, and an allowance of 147 basis points of commitments (10-Q Q3 page:34, page:37, page:88). The main business-model risks are the combination of rising leverage with continued buybacks and dividends, the concentration of refinancing in 2028, the dependence on lender discretion for secured credit agreement availability, and the manager conflicts described below.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

All items below are completed unless labelled as a subsequent event. There is no transaction source for a sponsor deal, merger or change of control, and none is inferred; the pack describes financing and portfolio activity only.

In May 2026 TRTX closed a 400.0 million secured Term Loan B at a price of 99.75, bearing Term SOFR plus 2.75%, maturing May 2033, with quarterly amortization of 0.25% of the original principal from the last business day of December 2026. Obligations are guaranteed by certain subsidiaries and secured on a first-priority basis by substantially all assets of the company and certain subsidiaries (10-Q Q3 page:56). The filing says the Term Loan B and the Revolver are used "to repay outstanding indebtedness and for other general corporate purposes" (page:55); which indebtedness was repaid is not itemized, although the Q3 filing links the May 2026 redemption of TRTX 2022-FL5 to an upsized Wells Fargo agreement (page:44). At the same time TRTX closed a 100.0 million Revolver at Term SOFR plus 2.00% maturing May 2031, undrawn at 2026-09-30 (page:57). A Credit Agreement dated 2026-05-14 with Wells Fargo Bank, N.A. and other lenders is listed as an exhibit to the Q2 2026 10-Q (10-Q Q2 page:133); the filings do not say which facility it governs and the text is not supplied. The company also paid TPG Capital BD, an affiliate of TPG, 0.9 million for capital markets services on these facilities (10-Q Q3 page:65). In September 2026 a 29.1 million first mortgage loan from BMO Harris Bank on the Plano multifamily property replaced an asset-specific financing after the underlying loan converted to real estate owned through a non-judicial foreclosure on September 1, 2026, which crystallized a 13.0 million realized loss (page:39, page:54).

After the quarter, as a subsequent event, TRTX closed TRTX 2026-FL8, a 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO, on October 2, 2026, placing approximately 820.0 million of investment-grade securities with institutional investors (10-Q Q3 page:74; release 2026-10-26 page:4). Supporting exhibits (indenture, collateral interest purchase agreement, collateral management agreement and servicing agreement) were filed with an 8-K of October 6, 2026 that is not in the pack (page:135). The use of proceeds, the collateral, the retained interest, any related redemption of other debt and the effect on the secured credit agreements are not stated. The liquidity effect of the CLO cannot be assessed; the 2026-09-30 balance sheet does not include it. Also as a subsequent event, repayments of 72.2 million were received, including a full repayment of 61.5 million (page:74), and on October 26, 2026 the board approved a new share repurchase program of up to 50.0 million of common stock, which management described as "doubling our prior authorization" (release 2026-10-26 page:2); this is Management Language, and the prior authorization was a 25.0 million program announced on September 4, 2025 (10-Q Q2 page:132). ### Credit view

TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. is a moderately leveraged, externally managed commercial real estate lender whose asset quality looks stable but whose cushions are narrowing. The strongest support is a senior, floating-rate loan book with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0, no non-accrual loans and commitments of USD 5,168.7 million, funded 78.8% without market-value margin calls. The weakest point is leverage: debt of USD 4,198.1 million against equity of USD 1,024.1 million gives 4.03x, above the 3.75:1 the company expected in its 10-K, with USD 52.6 million of cash tied up for covenants. What decides the outcome is whether loan repayments and the October 2026 CLO bring leverage and liquidity back toward the company's own range while earnings cover the dividend.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis | Limitation |

| Adequate fundamental credit quality with a weakening trend in leverage, liquidity and earnings cover; asset quality indicators stable | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; Funding structure and recourse; Liquidity; Covenants] [CP-1A: Credit translations; Governance and sponsor behaviour] | Confidence is below High because CP-1A judged this module ready with limitations, covenant values and executed agreements are not supplied, and the effect of the October 2026 CLO is unknown |
### Thesis

The lender's senior, floating-rate, mostly multifamily and industrial loan book and long-dated, largely non-marked funding support its credit quality, but a rise in leverage to 4.03x, thin usable liquidity and dividend cover below one after realized losses leave a narrowing cushion that depends on repayments and refinancing execution through 2028.
### Key findings

TPG RE Finance Trust, Inc. grew its balance sheet with debt in 2026, and that is the finding that matters most. Debt principal rose from USD 3,309.5 million at 2025-12-31 to USD 4,198.1 million at 2026-09-30, while stockholders' equity fell from USD 1,068.0 million to USD 1,024.1 million, so the company's own total leverage ratio rose from 3.02x to 4.03x and the debt-to-equity ratio excluding the Term Loan B from 3.02x to 3.64x. The 10-K had said the company expected total debt to equity to be generally below 3.75:1. On the ratio that includes the Term Loan B, TRTX is above that range; reducing net debt by about USD 286.8 million, or adding about USD 76.5 million of equity, would bring it back to 3.75x. The basis of the 3.75:1 expectation after the Term Loan B is not stated, so this is a pointer, not a breach [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Financials and credit metrics; CP-1A: logged difference on leverage expectation].

The company's funding became more corporate and more recourse. A USD 400.0 million Term Loan B at Term SOFR plus 2.75% maturing in May 2033 and an undrawn USD 100.0 million Revolver closed in May 2026; both are fully recourse, as is the USD 265.0 million secured revolving facility. Together with partial recourse to Holdco on the secured credit agreements, nominal recourse exposure is USD 1,051.7 million, about 1.03 times equity, and the cash the company holds for its liquidity covenant, USD 52.6 million, is consistent with five percent of that exposure. Against this, 45.7% of debt is non-recourse CRE CLO debt and 78.8% is not subject to market-value margin calls [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse].

Liquidity improved in headline terms but is thin in usable terms. Near-term liquidity of USD 291.6 million at 2026-09-30 compares with USD 143.0 million at 2025-12-31, but USD 52.6 million of the USD 70.8 million of cash is held for covenants, and only USD 87.3 million of the USD 777.8 million of secured credit agreement availability counts as available without pledging more collateral. After covenant cash, liquidity of about USD 239.0 million is about equal to USD 236.6 million of unfunded loan commitments [Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity].

Earnings softened in the latest quarter and cover of the dividend is below one after realized losses. Net income was USD 9.4 million in Q3 2026 against USD 22.0 million a year earlier, and net interest income fell 5.7%. Distributable Earnings before realized losses covered the common dividend 0.98 times in Q3 2026, but after the USD 13.0 million realized loss on a Plano foreclosure Distributable Earnings were USD 5.1 million against common dividends declared of USD 18.5 million, a cover of 0.28 times. Over nine months of 2026 they covered declared common dividends 0.98 times before and 0.75 times after realized losses, while the company also bought back shares for USD 24.6 million [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures; CP-1A: Governance].

Asset quality indicators remain stable but the book is transitional and growing. Weighted average risk rating is 3.0, no loan was on non-accrual at 2026-09-30, and the allowance is 147 bp of commitments, or USD 76.1 million. Multifamily and industrial are 75.2% of commitments and loans are 99.7% floating rate. Offsetting this, 64.0% of commitments are bridge loans, seven real estate owned properties are held after a September 2026 foreclosure, and office exposure rose from 4.3% to 7.9% after a USD 212.0 million San Francisco loan, after management said in April 2026 that office exposure was below 5% [Documentary Fact and Management Language; CP-1: Credit quality; CP-1A: logged difference on office exposure].

Refinancing risk is concentrated in 2028 and depends on extensions. Debt maturing in 2028 is USD 1,130.8 million, 26.9% of principal, including USD 792.6 million of secured credit agreements and USD 265.0 million of the secured revolver; CLO maturities follow loan repayments. A USD 1.0 billion managed CRE CLO closed on 2026-10-02, after the balance sheet date, with about USD 820.0 million of investment-grade notes placed, but its use of proceeds is not disclosed, so its effect on leverage and recourse is unknown [Documentary Fact; CP-1: Chart data: debt maturities; CP-1A: Transaction summary].
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strength: collateral quality indicators. The loan book is entirely senior first mortgage loans, with a weighted average risk rating of 3.0 unchanged since 2025-12-31, no non-accrual loans, a weighted average loan-to-value of 65.9% at origination and an allowance of 147 bp of commitments. The mechanism is that senior, floating-rate lending with interest rate floors protects income and gives asset-level lenders collateral cover; the implication is limited realized losses so far (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Credit quality). The loan-to-value is an underwriting measure, not a current valuation.

Strength: funding structure. 78.8% of debt is not subject to market-value margin calls, 45.7% is non-recourse CLO debt isolated from parent assets, the Term Loan B runs to May 2033 and the Revolver to May 2031, and secured credit agreement lenders are four banks. The mechanism is that forced deleveraging through margin calls is limited and term funding is long; the implication is lower exposure to market-value margin calls, although the secured credit agreements remain repurchase-style borrowings with credit marks (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Funding structure and recourse).

Strength: disclosure and interest rate positioning. The company publishes a loan-by-loan schedule, risk ratings, recourse by facility and a liquidity table, and a 25 bp rise in rates adds about USD 2.9 million to annual net interest income because net floating-rate exposure is USD 1,186.2 million. The implication is good monitorability and a positive rate sensitivity (Documentary Fact; CP-1A: Company and operating model).

Weakness: leverage and thin equity cushion. Total leverage of 4.03x is above the 10-K's 3.75:1 expectation, equity fell 4.1% in nine months, and the indicative ratio of debt principal to total assets is 80.1% against a covenant maximum of 83.333%; assets could fall by only about USD 205.2 million, or 3.9%, before that indicative ratio reaches the maximum. The mechanism is that realized and provisioned losses reduce equity directly while debt is fixed; the implication is limited tolerance for credit losses before covenant pressure, subject to the unsupplied covenant definition (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Covenants, Calculations).

Weakness: usable liquidity and lender discretion. Cash tied to covenants rises with each draw on recourse debt, secured credit agreement availability depends on lender-approved collateral, and unfunded commitments are USD 236.6 million. The mechanism is that liquidity can shrink when repayments slow or when the recourse base grows; the implication is dependence on repayments and the October 2026 CLO for headroom (Analyst Interpretation; CP-1: Liquidity).

Weakness: earnings cover and distributions. Dividends and buybacks exceeded earnings after realized losses in Q3 2026, and nine-month Distributable Earnings of USD 42.3 million were below declared common dividends of USD 56.7 million. The mechanism is that distributions drawn from equity reduce the cushion beneath creditors; the implication is that continued distributions at this level depend on earnings recovery (Documentary Fact; CP-1: Earnings measures).

Weakness: external management and affiliate arrangements. The manager earns 1.50% of Equity as defined regardless of performance, the fee base implied by the Q3 2026 fee exceeds stockholders' equity, three of eight directors are TPG employees and affiliate payments are disclosed but small. The mechanism is that the manager's income does not fall with credit losses; the implication is indirect alignment with creditors and no documented sponsor support (Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; CP-1A: Ownership and control, Governance).

Weakness: missing measures. EBITDA, covenant ratio values and executed agreements are not available, so leverage and coverage on lender definitions cannot be tested (Insufficient Information; limitation stated in the gaps).

Overall, evidence traceability is Ready with Remediation. Of the Top 5 material credit drivers, 3 are directly sourced, 2 are calculated, 0 are assumption-based, 0 are analyst inferences, and 0 are weak-lineage, untraced, conflicting, or insufficient-information items. The most important provenance gap is the absence of covenant test values and executed credit agreements, which matters because covenant headroom, the recourse base and the guarantor package can then be read only from filing summaries and inference, and it implies that committee use stays restricted until they are supplied. The unsupported claim to correct is that the loan book is entirely senior first mortgage loans; the affected decision is leverage tolerance; the remediation owner is the sourcing step.
